content.text:
Start working on Linear ticket eng-2478 based off eng-893. app: Obsidian by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `eng-2478 based off eng-893. app: Obsidian` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `eng-2478 based off eng-893. app: Obsidian`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

The copied `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH` points at the main checkout's vault. Step 7 replaces it
with the vault leased to this worktree.

### 6c. Link the shared `dg-*` and `scope-check` skills into the worktree

Claude Code only loads skills from `.claude/skills`, but the repo's shared skills live in
`.agents/skills`. Without this step they never load in the worktree: they cannot trigger on
their own descriptions and have no slash command.

Run from the main repo root, substituting the worktree path:

```bash
WT=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>"
MAIN="$PWD"
mkdir -p "$WT/.claude/skills"
# scope-check isn't dg-prefixed but the PR flow needs it as a Skill call.
for src in "$MAIN"/.agents/skills/dg-*/ "$MAIN"/.agents/skills/scope-check/; do
  [ -d "$src" ] || continue
  s=$(basename "$src")
  if [ -d "$WT/.agents/skills/$s" ]; then
    # Relative link, so the worktree uses its own branch's copy of the skill.
    ln -sfn "../../.agents/skills/$s" "$WT/.claude/skills/$s"
  else
    # Branch predates the skill; fall back to the main checkout's copy.
    ln -sfn "$MAIN/.agents/skills/$s" "$WT/.claude/skills/$s"
  fi
done
ls -l "$WT/.claude/skills/"
```

Verify each link resolves before moving on:

```bash
for d in "$WT"/.claude/skills/dg-* "$WT"/.claude/skills/scope-check; do
  [ -f "$d/SKILL.md" ] || echo "BROKEN: $d"
done
```

These links are gitignored (`.claude/*`), so they are local to this machine and add nothing
to the diff. Use a glob rather than a variable list: zsh does not word-split unquoted
variables, so `for s in $SKILLS` silently iterates once with the whole string.

### 6d. Local Supabase runs natively, not in Docker

Anything that needs a local database (`SUPABASE_USE_DB=local`, `pnpm -C <worktree>/packages/database dev`)
goes through the CLI's native stack, so Docker Desktop does not need to be running. Requires CLI >= 2.122.

Export this before any command that may start Supabase:

```bash
export SUPABASE_EXPERIMENTAL_STACK=1
```

The env var is the lever here, not `config.toml`. The `[experimental] stack = true` key is tracked
per branch, so a worktree cut from `origin/main` does not have it until it is committed there.

Notes:
- `packages/database/scripts/serve.ts` shells out to a bare `supabase start`, so the env var is the
  only way to reach it. For commands you run directly, `supabase start --runtime native` is explicit.
- Stack identity keys on `project_id`, which is the same in every worktree. All worktrees therefore
  share one local stack, exactly as they shared one Docker stack. Pass `--stack <branch-name>` only
  if the ticket genuinely needs an isolated database.
- The stack is alpha and excluded from the CLI compatibility promise. If it fails, start Docker
  Desktop and rerun without the env var to fall back.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `SUPABASE_USE_DB=none pnpm -C <worktree>/apps/roam dev`
- **Obsidian**: `node ~/.claude/skills/obsidian-vault/scripts/vault.mjs dev --worktree <worktree>`
  - This leases a free local-db vault and writes `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH` and `SUPABASE_USE_DB` for
    it into `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env`. It then starts the watcher. A later plain `pnpm dev`
    and CDP runs use the same vault. Add `--db production` only if the user asks to test against
    prod (testVault123).
  - For **None**, still run `vault.mjs claim --worktree <worktree>` if the ticket touches
    apps/obsidian, so the `.env` doesn't keep pointing at the main checkout's vault.
  - **Exit 2** means every vault in that pool is taken. Follow the `obsidian-vault` skill: ask the
    user which vault to take over, then rerun with `--take <vault>`. Never pick one yourself.
  - On success, pass the printed `obsidian://open?path=` URL to the user, so they open that vault.
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn <worktree>/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

**Dev server gotchas** (learned the hard way — don't rediscover these):

- The filter flag is `--filter`, not `--F`. Turbo 2.5.6 rejects `--F=roam` outright.
- Prefer `pnpm -C <abs-path> <app> dev` over `turbo dev --filter=<app>`. `turbo dev --filter=roam`
  also runs the `@repo/database#dev` dependency, which needs a local Supabase plus an explicit
  `SUPABASE_USE_DB`; if that fails turbo fails the *entire* run even though the app itself built
  fine. Going through `pnpm -C` skips the dependency graph.
- `SUPABASE_USE_DB` must be one of `local | branch | production | none | implicit`
  (see `packages/database/src/dbDotEnv.mjs`). Use `none` for work that doesn't touch the database.
- **Always bake the absolute worktree path into the command.** The Bash tool's cwd resets to the
  main repo between calls, so a backgrounded `pnpm --filter roam dev` with no path silently builds
  the *main repo's* `dist` — not the worktree the symlink points at. `pnpm -C <abs-path>` makes the
  path intrinsic to the command so it can't be dropped.
- After starting, verify before reporting success: confirm the log says `built with 0 errors` **and**
  that `<worktree>/apps/roam/dist` has a fresh mtime. A background task that failed still returns a
  task ID.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, **read the `CONTEXT_FILE`** and load it as working context
  (`Next step`, `Open questions`, `Key decisions`, `Dead ends`).
- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=no` or the command errors, continue — this is a fresh start.

### 9. Show context
After setup, display:
- Ticket ID and title
- Branch name you're on
- Brief description from the ticket (if available)
- Which app dev server is running (if any), and for Obsidian, which vault is leased
- That the shared `dg-*` and `scope-check` skills are linked and resolving
- If prior session context was found: its `TL;DR` and `Next step`
- A short "ready to work" confirmation
- Remind the user they can run `/checkpoint` to save session context before wrapping up
I'll start by fetching the ticket details. Linear MCP needs auth — let me check what's available first.

The panel's own list is a Blueprint `Menu` inside a `max-h-48 overflow-y-auto` scroller, so with many types the panel scrolls rather than growing.

Focus: it never steals focus. The outer popover sets `autoFocus={false}`, and *every* interactive element in the header and panel carries `onMouseDown={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` — filter button, "Select all", each type `MenuItem`, and each "Only" button. The textarea keeps the caret and keeps receiving keystrokes the entire time. Toggling is pure click toggle; there's no outside-click handler scoped to the panel, so the panel closes only via the filter button again, via "Only" (item 4), or when the whole menu unmounts.

## 3. Checkbox list

Not real checkboxes — each row is a Blueprint `MenuItem` with `icon={null}` whose text is a flex row rendering a manual checkmark glyph:

```tsx
<span className="mr-2">{isSelected ? "✓" : " "}</span>
<span>{item.text}</span>
```

Initial state: **all types checked.** Set once on mount in `fetchNodeTypes`, over `getDiscourseNodes().filter((n) => n.backedBy === "user")`:

```tsx
const initialCheckedTypes: Record<string, boolean> = {};
allNodeTypes.forEach((t) => { initialCheckedTypes[t.type] = true; });
setCheckedTypes(initialCheckedTypes);
```

Clicking anywhere on the row toggles that one type (`handleTypeCheckChange` flips the boolean; `shouldDismissPopover={false}` plus `preventDefault/stopPropagation` keep both the panel and the outer menu open). Unchecking does two things, both via the `checkedTypes`-dependent effect and `filteredTypes`: the search is re-run with the narrowed `typeFilter`, and the type's section header disappears from the result list entirely (`filteredTypes` keeps only checked types that also have ≥1 result). Results re-render immediately — no debounce on filter changes (the 300 ms debounce applies only to typed search text).

Select all button, right side of the panel's own "Filter by Type" header row:

```tsx
<Button
  small
  intent={isAllSelected ? Intent.SUCCESS : Intent.PRIMARY}
  icon={isAllSelected ? "tick" : "multi-select"}
  onMouseDown={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
  onClick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); e.preventDefault();
    handleToggleAll(!isAllSelected); }}
>
  {isAllSelected ? "All selected" : "Select all"}
</Button>
```

`isAllSelected = typeIds.length > 0 && typeIds.every((id) => !!checkedTypes[id])`. So:
- Any type unchecked → label "Select all", `multi-select` icon, PRIMARY (blue) intent; clicking checks every type.
- All checked → label "All selected", `tick` icon, SUCCESS (green) intent; clicking **unchecks every type** (it's a toggle, not a no-op) — which lands you in the zero-selected state of item 6.

Note the panel has its own second header row, `"Filter by Type"` in `text-sm font-medium text-gray-700`, left of that button.

## 4. "Only"

Rendered inside every type row, hidden until hover: `className="... opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100"` (the `MenuItem` carries `className="group !p-0"`). It occupies the right edge of the row at full row height, so hovering a row reveals it in place without reflow. Its handler:

```tsx
onClick={(e) => {
  e.stopPropagation();
  handleSelectOnly(item);
  setIsFilterMenuVisible(false);
}}
```

`handleSelectOnly` replaces the whole selection map with exactly one true entry: `Object.fromEntries(typeIds.map((id) => [id, id === node.type]))`. So it is "check this, uncheck all others" in one step, regardless of prior state. `stopPropagation` stops the row's own toggle from also firing. And yes — it **collapses the filter panel** (`setIsFilterMenuVisible(false)`, ENG-1046's behaviour), leaving the results list showing just that one type's section, with the outer menu and textarea focus untouched.

## 5. Filter lifecycle

**Reset on every open, never remembered.** There is no persistence: `checkedTypes` is component state, initialized in the mount-time `useEffect(() => { fetchNodeTypes(); }, [])` (lines 208–262, the `initialCheckedTypes` snippet above). `isFilterMenuVisible` likewise starts `false` via `useState(false)`. The reset is structural: `renderDiscourseNodeSearchMenu` creates a fresh `<span>` parent and `ReactDOM.render`s a new `NodeSearchMenu` on every trigger, and `onClose` does `ReactDOM.unmountComponentAtNode(parent); parent.remove();`. So each summon rebuilds the MiniSearch index *and* the all-checked filter state from scratch. No extension setting, no `localStorage`, nothing carried across invocations (contrast with `NodeSearchMenuTriggerSetting`, which does persist, but that's only the trigger string).

## 6. How selection reaches the search, and zero-selected

One effect owns it:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  if (isLoading || !miniSearchRef.current) return;
  const selectedTypes = discourseTypes
    .filter((type) => checkedTypes[type.type])
    .map((type) => type.type);
  const newResults = searchWithMiniSearch(searchTerm, selectedTypes);
  setSearchResults(newResults);
}, [searchTerm, isLoading, discourseTypes, checkedTypes, searchWithMiniSearch]);
```

The selected type ids are passed as `typeFilter` into MiniSearch, in two modes:
- **Empty search term:** per selected type, `search.search(MiniSearch.wildcard, { filter: r => r.type === type })`, sliced to `MAX_ITEMS_PER_TYPE = 10`. So opening the menu with no query already shows up to 10 per checked type.
- **Non-empty term:** one `search(searchTerm, { fields: ["text"], ...DISCOURSE_NODE_MINI_SEARCH_OPTIONS, filter: r => typeFilter.includes(r.type) })`, then dropped below `DISCOURSE_NODE_MIN_SEARCH_SCORE`, then grouped by type and capped at 10 per type.

Filtering is applied at the search/ranking call, not post-hoc, so the 10-per-type cap is computed over the filtered set — narrowing types can surface lower-ranked items of the remaining type that were previously cut off.

Zero types selected → `selectedTypes` is `[]`, which is truthy, so `typeFilter` is an empty array (never `undefined`, so the "no filter" branch is unreachable from the UI): with an empty query the `forEach` loop produces `{}`; with a query, `[].includes(...)` is always false. Either way **results are empty, not all** — the list renders the fallback:

```tsx
{allItems.length === 0 && (
  <div className="p-3 text-center text-gray-500">No matches found</div>
)}
```

Same copy as a genuine no-match; there is no distinct "no types selected" message. Enter does nothing in that state (`if (allItems.length > 0)`).

## 7. Keyboard

There is **no keyboard interaction with the panel** — it is mouse-only. No arrow navigation among type rows, no Space/Enter to toggle a type, no tab stop reached (focus never leaves the textarea), no shortcut to open the filter panel.

All key handling is a listener bound to the textarea (or `textarea.parentElement` when inside `.rm-reference-item`), and it is unaffected by whether the panel is open:

- ArrowDown / ArrowUp: wrap-around move of `activeIndex` over `allItems` — the flattened *result* list, only while `allItems.length` is non-zero; both `preventDefault` + `stopPropagation` so Roam doesn't act on them. A separate effect scrolls the `data-active="true"` item into view with `block: "nearest"`.
- Enter: selects `allItems[activeIndex].item`, inserts `[[Title]]` at the trigger position, closes the menu.
- Escape: `onClose()` — closes the **entire** menu, not just the filter panel. There is no "Escape closes the panel first" step.

How the menu stays open while the panel is used: three mechanisms working together — `autoFocus={false}` on the popover plus `onMouseDown={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` on every control (clicks never blur the textarea, so the "textarea lost focus / input no longer matches trigger" close path never fires), `shouldDismissPopover={false}` on the type `MenuItem`s and the result `MenuItem`s (Blueprint would otherwise dismiss the enclosing popover on item click), and `e.stopPropagation()` on the filter/Select-all/Only handlers. Also note `useEffect(() => { if (activeIndex >= allItems.length) setActiveIndex(0); }, [allItems, activeIndex])` — after a filter change shrinks the list, the highlight snaps back to the first item rather than going out of range.

One more behavioural detail worth porting: the only close triggers are Escape, selecting an item, and `handleTextAreaInput` failing to match the trigger regex (i.e. the user deleted the trigger or moved the caret before it) — filter interactions are deliberately insulated from all of those.</result>

# ENG-2478 — Add a type filter panel to the Obsidian node summoning menu

## Context

ENG-893 builds the Obsidian node summoning menu as a custom React popover at the cursor:
typing the trigger (`@`) opens a list of discourse nodes grouped by type, capped at 10 per
type. It has no type filter, so Roam and Obsidian are not at parity, and in a vault with many
nodes the type a user wants can be pushed out of its 10-slot group by other types' results.

This ticket adds the header row ENG-893 deliberately left out, with a filter button that opens
a "Filter by Type" panel — checkbox per type, "Select all", and "Only" on hover — and threads
the selection into the ranking call.

This branch is stacked on `eng-893-implement-node-summoning-menu-in-obsidian`, so the PR
targets that branch, not `main`, and ENG-893 must merge first.

## Roam reference behaviour (the spec to mirror)

From `apps/roam/src/components/DiscourseNodeSearchMenu.tsx`. We mirror behaviour, not code —
Roam is BlueprintJS, Obsidian is not.

- **Header row**: one bordered row holding only an icon-only filter button, tooltip
  "Filter by type". No active-filter indicator — no badge, no count, no restyling when a
  subset is selected.
- **Panel**: an inline panel in normal flow under the header, above the results. The results
  list keeps its own fixed-height scroll box and stays visible. The panel's own list scrolls
  (`max-h-48`) rather than growing. It is not a nested popover.
- **Focus**: never stolen from the editor. Every control in the header and panel calls
  `preventDefault()` on `mousedown`, so the caret never moves and the close-on-blur path
  never fires.
- **Checkboxes**: all types start checked. Clicking a row toggles one type; its group
  disappears from the results immediately.
- **Select all**: label reads "Select all" when any type is unchecked, "All selected" when
  every type is checked.
- **Only**: hidden until row hover, revealed in place. Sets the selection to exactly that
  type and collapses the panel (ENG-1046).
- **Lifecycle**: reset to all-checked every time the menu opens. Never persisted.
- **Filtering point**: the selection is passed *into* the search/ranking call, not applied
  after, so the 10-per-type cap is computed over the filtered set — narrowing types can
  surface items that were previously cut off.
- **Keyboard**: the panel is mouse-only in Roam. Arrows/Enter act on results; Escape closes
  the whole menu, not just the panel.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

input.description:
## Problem

* Roam's summoning menu lets users narrow results to chosen node types (ENG-404, ENG-1046). The Obsidian menu from ENG-893 has no type filter.
* Without the filter, Obsidian is not at parity with Roam. In vaults with many nodes, a type the user wants can be pushed out of the 10-per-type list by other types' results.

## Solution

* Add a filter button to the menu header. The button opens a filter panel inside the menu, with a checkbox for each node type and an "Only" action on hover.
* Split `NodeTypeFilterMenu` so its panel can render inline. Advanced search keeps the dropdown, and the summoning menu renders the panel inside the menu.
* Pass the selected types to `rankDiscourseNodesByTitle` through `nodeTypeIds`.

## Done When

- [ ] The menu header has a filter button. Clicking it opens the filter panel inside the menu, without closing the menu or moving focus out of the editor.
- [ ] All types start checked. Unchecking a type removes its group from the results.
- [ ] "Only" selects just that type and collapses the filter panel (ENG-1046).
- [ ] When a filter is active, the filter panel shows "Clear filter (N)", where N is the number of checked types. Clicking it checks every type again.
- [ ] The filter button shows as active when a filter is active.
- [ ] Unchecking the last checked type returns to all types, as in advanced search.
- [ ] The filter resets to all types each time the menu opens.
- [ ] Typing after the trigger still narrows results inside the filtered types.
- [ ] Advanced search's type filter looks and works as before.

## Out of Scope

* Keyboard type filtering (FEE-278). Roam doesn't have it.
* Remembering the filter between openings. Roam doesn't do this.
* A setting for which types appear in the menu (ENG-2226 covers this for Roam).

## Notes

* ENG-893 builds the menu as a custom React popover without a header row. This ticket adds the header row and the filter button. ENG-893 doesn't use `EditorSuggest`, because its public API has no access to the popup element.
* The filter panel opens inside the menu. Don't use an Obsidian `Menu`, because that would take focus away from the editor.
* The summoning menu uses advanced search's "Clear filter (N)" instead of Roam's "Select all", so the two Obsidian filters match.
* The inline filter panel has no type search box. The box needs focus, which would take focus away from the editor. Roam's panel has no search box either.
* Roam reference: `apps/roam/src/components/DiscourseNodeSearchMenu.tsx` (filter panel and Only).
* Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

**The split:** [NodeTypeFilterMenu.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeTypeFilterMenu.tsx) now exports `NodeTypeFilterPanel`.
- It takes the same selected ids as the rest of the app, where `[]` means all types.

- Opening the filter shows 12 checked rows and no Clear filter button.
- "Only" keeps the panel open and shows "Clear filter (1)" and the badge.

**Checks:** ESLint is clean. `check-types` reports 34 errors, all in tldraw canvas files I didn't touch, and all "not a valid JSX element type". That looks like a React types mismatch in this worktree's `node_modules`, not something this change caused. CI should confirm it.

**To check it yourself** in testVault2 (`obsidian://open?path=%2FUsers%2Ftrang.doan%2FDocuments%2FtestVault2`):
1. Open advanced node search and click the filter icon. Every type should be checked, with a "Filter types…" box above the list.
2. Hover a row and click "Only". The panel should stay open, with "Clear filter (1)" at the top and a "1" badge on the icon.

content.text:
The type filter now works in the summoning menu and is ready for you to try. All 8 checks passed in testVault2. Nothing is committed.

**What changed:**
- [nodeSummonResults.ts](apps/obsidian/src/utils/nodeSummonResults.ts) takes the selected types and passes them to the existing ranking, so results are filtered before they're scored. I added two unit tests: one where an unchecked type's group disappears, and one where an empty selection keeps every group.
- [NodeSummonMenu.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSummonMenu.tsx) has a filter button at the top right of the menu. Clicking it opens the panel inside the menu, above the results.
  - The button is highlighted while the panel is open or a filter is on.
  - "Only" closes the panel.
  - Picking a type moves the highlight back to the first result.
  - The filter starts with every type each time the menu opens.
  - I didn't need to change the keyboard, focus or click-outside handling.

**Checks:**
- The 8 Obsidian checks clicked with real mouse events. They covered:
  - Opening the panel keeps the menu open and the cursor in the note.
  - Unchecking a type removes its group.
  - "Only" closes the panel and leaves one group.
  - "Clear filter (1)" brings every group back.
  - Unchecking every type shows all types.
  - Typing narrows results within the filter.
  - Reopening the menu resets the filter.
  - The arrow keys and Enter still insert a link while the panel is open.
- The typing check only partly proves narrowing: I typed "QUE", which matched all 10 Question results, so the count didn't drop. It still showed that the typing reached the note and that only the filtered type appeared.
- Unit tests (244) and lint pass. `check-types` still reports only the 34 tldraw errors from before.

**Two things to look at in the screenshots:**
- With the panel open, only about 2 results fit below it, because the menu keeps its usual maximum height.
- The filter button sits alone on its own row, and the menu gets narrower once a filter shortens the list.

Both look acceptable to me, but tell me if either bothers you.

**To try it** in testVault2: in any note, type `@`, then:
1. Click the filter icon. The cursor should stay in the note.
2. Uncheck a type. Its group should disappear.
3. Click "Only" on another type. The panel should close.
4. Reopen the panel and click "Clear filter".
5. Press Escape and type `@` again. Every type should be back.
Looks good, continue

input.ask: Should I fix the filter button jumping when the menu opens upward?

content.text:
The draft PR is open: [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1626](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1626), targeting `eng-893-implement-node-summoning-menu-in-obsidian`. It has one commit, `c7e847f1`. CI so far: 2 checks passed, 1 skipped, and none failed.

The PR hook wouldn't accept check runs from before the commit, so I ran `scope-check`, `dg-pr-adherence-check` and `dg-delegated-full-review` again on `c7e847f1`. Scope stays within Done When, and the standards check found nothing new in the code.

**What the second review found:**
- **Worth fixing (medium):** when the menu opens *above* the cursor, opening or closing the panel changes the menu's height. The menu moves to keep its bottom edge, so the filter button jumps and a second click can miss it. Near the edge of the window, the menu can also switch from below the cursor to above it mid-interaction. The likely fix is to keep the direction chosen when the menu opened and to anchor an upward menu by its bottom edge. That's a change to ENG-893's placement code, which is why I'm asking first.
- **Already decided:**
  - Escape closes the whole menu, not just the panel. That matches Roam, and keyboard filtering is out of scope.
  - The open panel leaves room for only about 2 results. You saw this in the screenshots and were fine with it.
  - There's no type search box inline.
- **Low, left as is:**
  - When the filter hides every match, the menu shows the general "No matching nodes" message.
  - The filter button still shows when no node types are set up.
  - If a node type is deleted while the menu is open, the filter can show as off while still hiding a group.
  - The panel's "Clear filter" focus handling does nothing inside the menu, which is harmless.
  - The filter icon is redrawn on every render.

**Still yours before marking it ready:**
- Add the Loom. The PR body says it's coming.
- Move ENG-2478 out of `Ticket Draft`.
- ENG-893 ([DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1617](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1617)) has to merge first.
So Rome currently have this jump behavior. What is a alternative behavior that you would suggest is a good way to move forward?

Here's what I'd suggest: **choose the direction once, when the menu opens, and pin the menu by the edge closest to the cursor.** Then the menu only ever grows away from the line you're typing on.

**What jumps today, in both Roam and our version:**
1. Every resize recalculates the menu's position from its new height. A menu that opens upward is placed by its top edge, so when the panel adds about 160px, the whole menu moves up by that much.
2. Near the bottom of the window, the extra height can make the menu flip from below the cursor to above it in the middle of an interaction. That's the worse of the two, because the whole menu moves to a different place.

**With the change:**
- **Menu below the cursor** (the usual case): the top edge stays put, the panel pushes the results down, and the filter button doesn't move. That's the same as today.
- **Menu above the cursor:** the bottom edge stays just above the cursor line, and the menu grows upward. The results stay next to the text you're typing, and the menu never flips while it's open.
- The trade-off: in the above-the-cursor case, the filter button is still at the top, so it moves up as the panel opens. You'd have to move the pointer to close the panel with the button. "Only" closes the panel by itself, so that's less of a problem in practice.

**If you want the button to stay put in both directions,** the header row has to sit on the cursor side. In an upward menu, it would sit at the bottom, with the panel opening above it. That gives no movement at all, but the menu's layout would differ by direction and from Roam, so I don't think it's worth it.

**Another option:** open the panel *over* the results instead of above them, so the menu's height never changes. Nothing moves, but you can't watch groups disappear as you uncheck types, and that live feedback is most of what makes the panel useful.

The change I'm suggesting is small: a direction field set on the first placement, plus a bottom-edge placement for upward menus. It lives in ENG-893's placement code, so it also fixes the flip for plain typing, where the result list grows or shrinks near the bottom of the window. If you'd rather keep Roam's behaviour exactly, leaving it as is is fine too.

content.text:
Yes, that was the cause. While a CDP check is running, the verify skill hid the whole Obsidian app every 1.5 seconds. All vaults share one Obsidian app, so a check from any session hid your window too, including the other worktree session that runs checks on "Obsidian Vault". From your side, that looked like Obsidian closing.

**What I changed** in your personal `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` skill:
- It never hides Obsidian by default.
- Obsidian still starts in the background (`open -g`). If starting it or opening a vault brings Obsidian to the front, the run switches back once to the app you were using. If you were already in Obsidian, it's left alone.
- Hiding is now opt-in with `--hide`, instead of opt-out with `--no-hide`. The skill's docs say the same.

**Proof:** I made Obsidian visible again, since earlier runs had left it hidden, and ran a check. Obsidian stayed visible the whole time and never came to the front. The check still passed.

# DG Create Engineering Ticket

Create an Engineering ticket that another engineer can understand and implement without rediscovering its intent or scope.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. It is in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

## Canonical template

The canonical Linear template is [General Engineering Task](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/new?template=6ca39698-3bce-449a-992e-059f0334e15b). Keep this link only as a reference in this skill. Never add it to a created ticket.

Use this exact template as the drafting checklist:

```markdown
## Problem

- What accepted user, developer, or project need does this address?
- Why does it need to be solved now?

## Solution

- What is the smallest change that solves the problem?

## Done When

- Describe how success is verified (behavioral or technical).
- Remember: Make only the smallest change needed to solve the problem.
- Remember: **Stay within the defined scope, or communicate any scope increase**

## Out of Scope

- (Optional) What adjacent cases, abstractions, or future work are explicitly not included?
- Link follow-up tickets where applicable

## Notes

- Additional Context, Blockers, dependencies, or follow-up actions.
```

Every bullet above is placeholder guidance. Replace or remove every placeholder before presenting a draft or creating a ticket. Keep all five headings, leaving `Out of Scope` or `Notes` empty when nothing useful applies. Use 1–3 short bullets per section unless the ticket is genuinely complex.

## Agent provenance and human review

Always use the Engineering team. This skill never creates or redirects to Feedback.

- Create every agent-created ticket in the existing `Ticket Draft` status with exactly one existing workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group. The label records provenance and stays after approval.
- Select the label from the creating agent's known identity: `Created by Claude` for Claude, `Created by Codex` for Codex, or `Created by LLM` for any other agent or when its identity cannot be determined. Do not infer agent identity from the Linear account, ticket topic, or skill name. Do not use `Created by LLM` as a substitute when the correct agent-specific label is missing.
- `Ticket Draft` is in the Backlog category and means human ticket review is pending; it does not authorize implementation. The existing `Draft` status belongs to the Started category and is used by the PR workflow. Do not use it for ticket review or change its automation.
- In `Notes`, record `Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket` and any other creation skills actually used. Skill attribution is provenance, not evidence that the ticket meets the standards.
- The human who asked the agent to create the ticket checks intent against the source request, scope and exclusions, verifiable acceptance criteria, and the canonical template and engineering writing standards. Keep the ticket in `Ticket Draft` while changes are needed.
- Human approval moves the ticket to `Backlog` when the problem and fix are agreed and implementation needs no further product or solution decisions. Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but decisions remain. Keep idea-stage Engineering requests in Engineering.
- The human's move from `Ticket Draft` to `Triage` or `Backlog` records sign-off. An agent may make that move only after explicit human approval of the completed ticket and destination. A request to create a ticket is not approval of its generated contents. Keep the provenance label and skill attribution.

## Project selection

Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Obsidian work with no relevant project, leave the project empty and apply the existing `Obsidian plugin` label. Do not use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`; the Obsidian queue picks up unprojected issues by label (see DIS-617).
4. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Any project you select must exist, not be completed, canceled, archived, or trashed, and include the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one. Obsidian tickets that do belong to a real project still use that project, plus the `Obsidian plugin` label.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label. Always apply `Obsidian plugin` to Obsidian work, since it is how unprojected Obsidian tickets reach the queue.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain optional labels do not block creation. If `Ticket Draft`, the required provenance label, or `Obsidian plugin` for Obsidian work is missing or ambiguous, return the prepared draft and report the configuration gap instead of creating an unmarked ticket or substituting a status.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description (including skill attribution), `Ticket Draft` status, project (omitted for unprojected Obsidian work), provenance and relevant labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

Read the created issue back and verify its status, labels, and attribution. For unprojected Obsidian work, confirm the project is empty and `Obsidian plugin` is applied. Report any mismatch instead of claiming successful routing. Return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link, and say that human review is pending. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

# Update Docs

Auto-update user-facing documentation when a feature or behavior change ships.
If `$ARGUMENTS` is provided, treat it as a GitHub PR number. Use `gh pr view $ARGUMENTS` to get the PR diff, changed files, and description. Use this instead of the current branch context.

If no argument is provided, use the current branch's diff against main, commit messages, and any linked Linear ticket to determine what changed.

## Guardrails

- Edit live docs only under `apps/website/content/**`.
- Put Obsidian docs under `apps/website/content/obsidian/**`.
- Put Roam docs under `apps/website/content/roam/**`.
- Do not edit legacy docs route shells or deleted legacy docs paths such as `apps/website/app/(docs)/docs/*/pages`, `docMap.ts`, `navigation.ts`, or `sharedPages`.
- Do not update runtime code, app routes, or package interfaces unless the dev explicitly asks for that separately.
- Use existing Nextra Markdown, MDX, and `nextra/components` features before proposing custom styling or layout.
- Use the existing global `NodeTag` MDX component for discourse candidate tag pills, such as `<NodeTag type="clm" />`. Allowed `type` values are `que`, `clm`, `evd`, `src`, `hyp`, `res`, and `iss`. Do not create one-off tag styling or CSS in docs content.
- Do not add or change theme, layout, route, component, or CSS code while adding documentation content. If existing Nextra features are not enough, flag the author to create a separate Linear ticket for new Nextra functionality.

## When to Run

On demand. Two modes:

- **Current branch** - Run while on a feature branch that's ready for PR or review.
- **Merged PR** - Pass a PR number to generate docs for an already-merged PR that's missing documentation.

## Step 1: Gather Context

### If running for the current branch

Collect information from three sources:

1. **Changed files** - Run `git diff main...HEAD --name-only` to identify what changed. Use file paths to determine the affected platform (see [scope-detection.md](references/scope-detection.md) for mapping).
2. **Commit messages** - Run `git log main...HEAD --oneline` for a summary of what was done.
3. **Linear ticket** - If a Linear ticket is linked by branch name or PR description, pull the title, description, and acceptance criteria for additional context. Use the Linear connector if available. If it is not available, prompt the dev to install Linear MCP using these instructions: https://linear.app/docs/mcp

### If running for a merged PR

Use the PR number to gather context via `gh`:

1. **PR details** - Run `gh pr view <PR_NUMBER>` to get the title, description, and linked issues.
2. **Changed files** - Run `gh pr diff <PR_NUMBER> --name-only` to identify what changed. Use file paths to determine the affected platform.
3. **Linear ticket** - If a Linear ticket is referenced in the PR title, branch name, or description, pull additional context from it.

## Step 2: Determine If Docs Are Needed

Apply the scope detection heuristic. See [scope-detection.md](references/scope-detection.md) for the full yes/no lists and file path to platform mapping.

If no docs update is needed, inform the dev and stop.

## Step 3: New Page vs Update Existing

1. Search existing docs only under `apps/website/content/**`.
2. Prefer updating an existing page when the change extends or corrects an already-documented feature.
3. Create a new page when the feature or workflow has no natural existing home.
4. If multiple plausible homes exist, ask the dev which page or section should own the content.

Defaults:

- Completely new feature with no existing coverage -> new page.
- Extending or modifying an already-documented feature -> update the existing page.
- Change applies to both platforms -> update both platform docs unless the existing docs already share a conceptual page through both sidebars.

## Step 4: Write or Update the Doc

Follow the formatting rules in [doc-conventions.md](references/doc-conventions.md).

For an **existing page**:

1. Edit the Markdown or MDX file under the relevant `apps/website/content/**` path.
2. Preserve existing frontmatter and local style.
3. Verify any new links point to live docs routes or existing files.

For a **new page**:

1. Choose the correct platform and section directory, such as `apps/website/content/obsidian/core-features/` or `apps/website/content/roam/guides/`.
2. Add a kebab-case `.md` or `.mdx` file with frontmatter.
3. Add the page slug to the nearest `_meta.ts` file so it appears in the sidebar. See [navigation-mapping.md](references/navigation-mapping.md).
4. Update `apps/website/docsRouteMap.ts` only when a flat legacy redirect like `/docs/<platform>/<slug>` should continue to resolve to the new sectioned route.

## Step 5: Verification

1. Present the draft changes to the dev for review.
2. List any screenshots that still need to be captured.
3. Flag broken cross-links, missing route map redirects, or stale content observed while editing.
4. Leave all changes as unstaged modifications. The dev reviews and commits themselves.

**Node search** is a dedicated surface to search and interact with discourse nodes in your vault.

## Open the search

1. Open the command palette with `Cmd/Ctrl + P`
2. Search for "node search" and select **Discourse Graph: Open node search**

![Node search modal with ranked results and a preview](/docs/obsidian/node-search-results.png)

## Filter by node type

There are two ways to narrow results to particular node types. Both drive the same filter, so you can start with one and finish with the other.

### From the filter dropdown

Click the funnel icon to the right of the search field and tick the node types you want.

![Node type filter dropdown](/docs/obsidian/node-search-type-filter.png)

- **Only** — appears when you hover or focus a row, and narrows the filter to that single type
- **Clear filter** — removes the filter entirely and shows the count of types currently selected
- A **Filter types…** box appears once you have more than seven node types configured, so a long list stays manageable

A badge on the funnel icon shows how many types are selected. Selecting every type is the same as selecting none — both show all your nodes.

### From the keyboard, as tag chips

Start typing a node type's name in the search field and its full name appears as ghost text with a `Tab` hint.

![Typing a node type name shows a Tab completion hint](/docs/obsidian/node-search-type-completion.png)

Press `Tab` to turn it into a chip. The search field clears so you can immediately type another type name, or start typing the title you're actually looking for.

![Two node type chips beside a search query](/docs/obsidian/node-search-type-chips.png)

## Sort the results

Click the sort icon to choose how results are ordered.

![Sort dropdown with five dimensions and direction toggle](/docs/obsidian/node-search-sort.png)

Notes with no resolvable author sort after every named author, in both directions.

## Act on a result

The footer shows what you can do with the highlighted result, and every action there is clickable as well as keyboard-driven.

| Action                                     | Shortcut       |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------- |
| Insert a link to the result at your cursor | `Cmd/Ctrl + ↵` |

# Documentation Conventions

## File locations

User-facing plugin docs live in the Nextra content tree:

- Obsidian: `apps/website/content/obsidian/**`
- Roam: `apps/website/content/roam/**`
- Blog posts: `apps/website/content/blog/**`
- Site-wide docs landing pages: `apps/website/content/**`

Do not create plugin docs outside `apps/website/content/**`.

## Filename convention

Use kebab-case for doc filenames, such as `creating-discourse-nodes.md`.
Use `.md` for normal prose pages and `.mdx` only when the page needs components.

## Frontmatter

Every plugin doc file should include this frontmatter block unless nearby files in the same section use a different required shape:

```yaml
---
title: "Page title"
date: "YYYY-MM-DD"
author: ""
published: true
---
```

Use sentence case for page titles unless the title includes an official product name, plugin name, or UI label.

## Nextra styling and formats

Use existing Nextra Markdown, MDX, and `nextra/components` features before proposing custom styling.

Good first choices include:

- Standard Markdown headings, lists, links, tables, and code fences
- Nextra `Callout` for warnings, tips, notes, and important context
- Nextra `Cards` for small sets of high-level navigation options
- Nextra `Steps` for ordered setup or workflow instructions
- Nextra `Tabs` for compact platform or mode variants
- Nextra `Table` and `FileTree` when structured data or file paths need clearer presentation
- The global `NodeTag` MDX component for discourse candidate tag pills, such as `<NodeTag type="clm" />`, `<NodeTag type="evd" />`, or `<NodeTag type="que" />`. Allowed `type` values are `que`, `clm`, `evd`, `src`, `hyp`, `res`, and `iss`.

Use `.mdx` when a page needs MDX components like `Callout`, `Image`, or `NodeTag`. `NodeTag` renders `#<type>-candidate` by default and uses the approved node colors. Do not import `NodeTag` in individual docs pages; it is registered globally through `mdx-components.tsx`.

Do not change docs structural code, theme files, route shells, app layouts, shared components, or CSS as part of adding content.
If the content needs a styling or presentation feature that existing Nextra features cannot support, stop and flag the author to create a separate Linear ticket for adding that Nextra functionality.

## Links

- Prefer absolute docs routes for cross-page links, such as `/docs/obsidian/core-features/node-tags`.
- Use relative links only when the target is in the same local section and the existing section already uses relative links.
- Verify every new link points to an existing file or route.
- Do not link to old flat routes when the current sectioned route is known.

## Screenshots and media

Place documentation images in `apps/website/public/docs/<platform>/`.

Use public paths in Markdown:

```markdown
<!-- TODO: Add screenshot of [describe the UI element or feature] -->
<!-- ![Screenshot placeholder](/docs/roam/my-image.png) -->
```

For UI changes or visual features:

- Use a real screenshot when one is available.
- If no screenshot is available, add an HTML TODO comment describing what should be captured.
- Tell the dev exactly which screenshots still need to be captured.

## Cross-link integrity

- When adding or updating cross-links (e.g., `[text](./other-page)`), verify that the target page exists.
- If a link target does not exist, flag it to the dev.

## Cross-platform content

If a change applies to both Obsidian and Roam, update both platform docs unless there is already a shared conceptual page surfaced from both sidebars.
Keep platform-specific commands, settings names, and screenshots in the relevant platform section.

## Side observations

If you notice stale or incorrect content unrelated to the current change, flag it as a side observation.
Do not silently fix unrelated docs content unless the dev asks you to broaden the scope.

---
title: "General settings"
date: "2025-06-27"
author: ""
published: true
---

The General settings page in the Discourse Graph plugin provides fundamental configuration options that affect how the plugin operates. Here are the available settings:

## Show IDs in frontmatter

This setting controls the visibility of identifiers in your note's frontmatter section.

- When enabled, node type IDs and relation type IDs will be visible in the frontmatter of your notes
- When disabled, these IDs will be hidden from view
- This can be useful if you prefer a cleaner frontmatter appearance while still maintaining the underlying structure

## Show discourse context overlay

This setting controls whether links to discourse nodes carry an inline badge showing how many relations the linked node has.

- When enabled, a badge appears after each link to a discourse node, in both Live Preview and Reading view
- Selecting a badge opens that node's discourse context in a popover, where you can review its relationships and add a new one
- A node with no relations shows a badge reading `0`, and its popover says "No discourse relation found"
- Links to notes that are not discourse nodes never show a badge
- When disabled, the badges are removed immediately; the [discourse context view](/docs/obsidian/core-features/discourse-context) remains available from the sidebar

## Discourse nodes folder path

This setting determines where new discourse nodes will be created in your vault.

- Specify a folder path where you want all new discourse nodes to be stored
- Leave the field empty to create nodes in the root folder of your vault
- You can use the folder suggester to easily navigate and select existing folders
- Example format: `folder1/folder2`

Changes to these settings will only take effect after clicking the "Save Changes" button. The interface will indicate when you have unsaved changes pending.

---
title: "Node summoning menu"
date: "2026-11-15"
author: ""
published: true
---

The **node summoning menu** lets you link to a discourse node without leaving the note you're writing. Type `@`, start typing a title, and pick the node from a list grouped by node type.

<!-- TODO: Add screenshot of the menu open under "@clai" in a note, showing results grouped by node type -->
<!-- ![Node summoning menu with results grouped by node type](/docs/obsidian/node-summoning-menu.png) -->

## Open the menu

Type `@` at the start of a line or after a space. The menu opens at your cursor. Keep typing to narrow the results by title.

- An `@` inside a word, such as `me@lab.org`, doesn't open the menu.
- The menu doesn't open inside code, frontmatter, links, math or comments.
- A space right after `@` closes the menu, so `@ the lab` stays plain text.

### Change the trigger

To use something other than `@`, open **Settings → Discourse Graph → General** and edit **Node search trigger**. The trigger can be up to 5 characters and can't contain spaces. Leave it empty to turn the menu off.

## Insert a link

Results appear under their node type, best matches first, with up to 10 nodes per type.

Click a result, or highlight it and press `↵`, to replace what you typed with a link to that node. The link uses the format set in Obsidian's **Files and links** settings.

| Action                       | Shortcut  |
| ---------------------------- | --------- |
| Move the highlight           | `↑` / `↓` |
| Insert the highlighted node  | `↵`       |
| Close the menu               | `Esc`     |

If nothing matches, the menu shows "No matching nodes", and `↵` closes it.

## Filter by node type

Click the funnel icon at the top of the menu. The type filter opens inside the menu, above the results, and your cursor stays in the note so you can keep typing.

<!-- TODO: Add screenshot of the menu with the type filter open above the results, one type unchecked -->
<!-- ![Type filter open inside the node summoning menu](/docs/obsidian/node-summoning-menu-type-filter.png) -->

- **Uncheck a type** to remove its group from the results.
- **Only** appears when you hover a row. It narrows the filter to that type and closes the filter.
- **Clear filter (N)** appears while a filter is active, where N is the number of types selected. It checks every type again.

The funnel icon is highlighted while the filter is open or active. Unchecking every type is the same as checking every type: both show all your nodes. The filter resets to all types each time the menu opens.

[Node search](/docs/obsidian/core-features/node-search) uses the same type filter, plus a search box for long lists of node types.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build] [--hide]
```

It runs claim → doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 no vault available or vault locked, 3 marker missing.

On exit 2 with `candidates`, follow the `obsidian-vault` skill: ask Trang which vault to take, then run `vault.mjs claim --take` and rerun.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- With no `--slot`, the vault is this worktree's `obsidian-vault` lease. `run.mjs` claims a free one if the worktree has no lease yet. This keeps the CDP run in the vault the worktree's watcher builds into.
- `--slot N` is a legacy override. It's a 1-based index into `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env` and bypasses leases, so use it only when Trang names a slot.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault. The vault URL is skipped when that vault is already open.
- The run never hides Obsidian: other vault windows may be in use (recording, manual testing). Obsidian is launched with `open -g`, and if the launch or the `obsidian://` URL raises it, focus goes back once to the app that was frontmost. CDP input and screenshots work on a background window. Pass `--hide` to also hide Obsidian for the whole run.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved vault, the lock and the Obsidian state. It exits 2 if the worktree has no lease, or if another live run holds the lock. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about other worktrees' apps/obsidian `dev.ts` watchers that mirror into this vault. Your own worktree's watcher builds the same code, so it isn't flagged.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |
| `waitFor` on an IIFE always times out | `evaluate` adds an outer `return` only when the code contains no `return`. An IIFE with an inner `return` evaluates to `undefined`, so write `return (() => { ... })()`. |
| A note written in `setup` is randomly missing from search results | Datacore indexes new files after the metadata cache, and the search loads through Datacore. After `writeNote`, also `waitFor` `dc.query("@page and exists(nodeTypeId)")` to include the path. |

title: "Node summoning menu"
date: "2026-11-15"
author: ""
published: true
---

The **node summoning menu** lets you link to a discourse node without leaving the note you're writing. Type `@`, start typing a title, and pick the node from a list grouped by node type.

![Node summoning menu with results grouped by node type](/docs/obsidian/node-summoning-menu.png)

## Open the menu

Type `@` at the start of a line or after a space. The menu opens at your cursor. Keep typing to narrow the results by title.

- An `@` inside a word, such as `me@lab.org`, doesn't open the menu.
- The menu doesn't open inside code, frontmatter, links, math or comments.
- A space right after `@` closes the menu, so `@ the lab` stays plain text.

### Change the trigger

To use something other than `@`, open **Settings → Discourse Graph → General** and edit **Node search trigger**. The trigger can be up to 5 characters and can't contain spaces. Leave it empty to turn the menu off.

## Insert a link

Results appear under their node type, best matches first, with up to 10 nodes per type.

Click a result, or highlight it and press `↵`, to replace what you typed with a link to that node. The link uses the format set in Obsidian's **Files and links** settings.

| Action                      | Shortcut  |
| --------------------------- | --------- |
| Move the highlight          | `↑` / `↓` |
| Insert the highlighted node | `↵`       |
| Close the menu              | `Esc`     |

If nothing matches, the menu shows "No matching nodes", and `↵` closes it.

## Filter by node type

Click the funnel icon at the top of the menu. The type filter opens inside the menu, above the results, and your cursor stays in the note so you can keep typing.

![Type filter open inside the node summoning menu, with Question unchecked](/docs/obsidian/node-summoning-menu-type-filter.png)

- **Uncheck a type** to remove its group from the results.
- **Only** appears when you hover a row. It narrows the filter to that type and closes the filter.
- **Clear filter (N)** appears while a filter is active, where N is the number of types selected. It checks every type again.

The funnel icon is highlighted while the filter is open or active. Unchecking every type is the same as checking every type: both show all your nodes. The filter resets to all types each time the menu opens.

[Node search](/docs/obsidian/core-features/node-search) uses the same type filter, plus a search box for long lists of node types.

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.


If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

The ENG-2478 conflicts are fixed. [#1626](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1626) is mergeable again, and its diff is back to just the ENG-2478 files. CI is still running on it.

**What caused the conflicts:** ENG-893 was squash-merged into main as a single commit. #1626 then switched its target to main, but its branch still had ENG-893's original commits. Git saw both versions add the same five files and reported conflicts on all of them.

**How I fixed it:**
- My first attempt was to rebase ENG-2478's commit onto main. That applied with no conflicts, unit tests passed (248/248) and ESLint was clean. But updating the PR that way needs a force-push, and the permission check blocked it.
- Instead, I merged main into the branch (merge commit 4d419438) and pushed normally, so no history was rewritten. I resolved each conflict to the rebased version I had just tested, and checked that the merge result is identical to it.
- `check-types` still shows the same tldraw canvas errors as before, which only happen on this machine. None are in this branch's files.

**Docs PR:** [#1640](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1640) is open as a draft on top of #1626.
- It needed no changes after the merge. It still shows only the 4 docs files and is mergeable, with 5 checks passing and 1 pending.
- Before opening it, I ran all three pre-PR checks on its final head:
  - Scope check: nothing beyond Done When.
  - Standards check: ran.
  - Full review: the first pass flagged two gaps that I fixed: the trigger can't contain the node tag hotkey, and results are ordered by your node types' configured order. The second pass found nothing.
- The website production build passes.
- Still on you before marking it ready: move ENG-2494 out of Ticket Draft, and either keep the body's note explaining there's no Loom for this docs-only PR or record one.
